chunks: Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from Muʿallā Abī ʿUthmān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
But whoever remits it as charity, then it is an expiation for him.
He عليه السلام said: Some of his sins are expiated according to the extent to which he pardoned in the case of intentional killing.

key_terms.الْعَمْدِ: intentional offense, here referring to deliberate killing or injury
key_terms.تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ: to forgo one’s claim as an act of charity
key_terms.ذُنُوبِهِ: his sins that are forgiven through this act
key_terms.كَفّٰارَةٌ لَهُ: an expiation for the one who pardons

ai.seo_question: What does the verse “But whoever remits it as charity, then it is an expiation for him” mean in Shiʿi hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur’anic phrase about remitting retaliation as charity, interpreting it to mean that such pardon becomes an expiation for the one who forgives. The degree of expiation corresponds to the extent of the forgiveness shown in a case of intentional injury or killing.
